Hon'ble Shri Justice Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal Order on Board 10.12.2024 1.

This appeal has been preferred by the Insurance Company under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, challenging the award dated 31.08.2016 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ambikapur, District Sarguja (C.G.) in Claim Case No.309/2015.
2.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ambikapur, District Sarguja
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The facts, necessary for disposal of the present appeal, in brief, are that on 04.06.2015, deceased Kailash was standing in his field after asking respondent No.7 Suresh Yadav to plough the field with his tractor.

At about 12.30 in the afternoon, respondent No.6 Panchan Singh while ploughing his field with the tractor owned by respondent no.7 Suresh Yadav and insured by the appellant insurance company drove the tractor rashly and negligently and hit Kailash who was standing in the field.
In the accident, Kailash suffered grievous injuries in his back & waist and his spinal cord was fractured.
He was immediately taken to District Hospital, Ambikapur from where he was shifted to Raipur where he died during treatment in the hospital on 24.08.2015.
The claimants who are the wife and children of the deceased preferred an application before the Tribunal claiming total compensation of Rs.34,70,000/-.

sentences.text:
2 3. Learned counsel for the appellant insurance company argued that the claimant witnesses Smt.
Banas Bai and Ram Bihari Yadav themselves have admitted in cross-examination that the deceased was sitting in the tractor-trolley at the time of accident and this fact is also mentioned in the First Information Report (Exhibit P-2).

In such a situation, the insurance conditions have been violated and the risk of the deceased is not covered by the insurance policy because the seating capacity of the tractor-trolley was for only a driver.
Thus, the Tribunal has erred in holding the insurance company liable for payment of compensation.
Therefore, the award in question be set aside and the insurance company be exonerated from the liability.
4. There is no representation on behalf of the respondents.

5. Heard learned counsel for the appellant insurance company and perused the record.
6.
It is clear from perusal of the record that the claimant witness Smt. Banas is not an eye witness to the incident and she has stated in her cross-examination that she has told what she had heard.
In such a situation, the appellant insurance company does not get any benefit from her statement that the deceased was riding in the tractor at the time of the accident.
7. The appellant insurance company, in discharge of its responsibility, has examined only Dusendra Kumar Verma, who is not an eye witness to the incident.
He has verified the policy Ex. D-1 and said that no premium was paid for any additional rider other than the driver.

This witness has presented the investigation report Exhibit D-3 given by Investigator Kanta Gaur on behalf of the Insurance company, but that report is not verified as the Investigator's statement was not recorded.

The Tribunal has also mentioned about the said report that the two witnesses whose statements were taken by the Investigator have also not stated that the deceased was riding in the tractor-trolley at the time of the accident.
Thus, the investigation report also has no support for the insurance company.

8. Learned Tribunal, on the basis of the statement of eye-witness Ram Bihari Yadav, has found that at the time of accident, the deceased was standing on the ridge/boundary of his field and getting the work done, which could not be refuted.

Insofar as it is mentioned in the First Information Report that at the time of accident, the deceased was travelling in the tractor trolley, that First Information Report Exhibit P-2 is a supporting evidence.
Even though it has been produced by the claimant party, but Bhola Ram, who got that First Information Report Exhibit P-2 written or the Police Officer who wrote it, has not been examined.
The First Information Report Exhibit P-2
has been registered on the basis of another written report and that written report is also not presented in the record.

In such a situation, on the basis of that FIR (Ex.P-2) which is not a substantive piece of evidence, the statement of eye- witness Ram Bihari Yadav cannot be refuted because Ram Bihari Yadav has been consistent in his statement that at the time of accident, deceased Kailash was standing with him on the ridge/boundary of his field and getting it ploughed by the tractor and due to the negligence of the tractor driver, the tractor climbed the ridge/boundary and the accident happened by toppling over Kailash.
On the basis of this statement, no error/illegality is found in the finding of the Tribunal holding the insurance company liable for payment of compensation.
